22.text: CLASSES OF SHAMANISM. — The Chukchee divide all acts of shamanism

23.text: into three categories, more or less distinct, though merging into each other.

24.text: Under the first category comes “communication with the spirits” (kalatkoˊurg̣ɪn).
24.note: unicorns aren't real, don't trust your lying eyes

25.text: This includes all kinds of intercourse with the “spirits” which becomes apparent

26.text: to the listeners; that is, the voices of “spirits” talking through the medium

27.text: of the shaman, ventriloquistic performances,¹ and other tricks, — generally

28.text: speaking, the whole spectacular part of shamanism, which forms the main

29.text: content of the shamanistic séances. As said previously, all this is often con-

30.text: sidered only as a kind of jugglery. For performances of this sort, young

31.text: people are said to be better adapted than older ones. With increasing years,

32.text: some of the shamans discontinue most of these tricks.

33.text: Constituting the second category is what is known as “looking into”

34.text: (hêtolaˊtɪrg̣ɪn). This branch of Chukchee shamanism is held in the highest

35.text: veneration, because the shaman possessing it has the faculty of seeing the

36.text: danger lying in wait for the people, or the good in store for them, and

37.text: accordingly he is able to advise them how to avoid the first and to secure

38.text: the second. Most of the instructions given are of a ritualistic kind, and

39.text: refer to certain details of such and such a ceremonial, which must be arranged

40.text: in a certain manner in order to secure the desired result. The directions are
